artifacts.summary: Closes the --depends-on-add admission gap for not_started tasks via a new no-op-only preflight:edge_only pair in update-task-status.sh, full test coverage, suggester integration, doc update, and a live end-to-end proof (task 438 now depends on task 500).

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a dedicated no-op-only preflight:edge_only operation:target_status pair to update-task-status.sh so --depends-on-add can finally backfill an edge onto a not_started task, with full guarantee-preservation test coverage (Case 18, 7 sub-cases), suggester integration (orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh no longer falls back to propose-only for a not_started collision), a one-paragraph doc addition, and a live end-to-end proof: task 438's dependencies[] now includes 500, status unchanged at not_started.

memory_candidates.content: When a status-no-op-only operation:target_status pair is needed for a status no real transition produces (e.g. backfilling an edge onto a 'not_started' task), mint a dedicated literal-named pair (e.g. preflight:edge_only) that resolves STATE_STATUS to that literal status, gate it preflight-only alongside similar human/tooling-initiated pairs (hold/unhold), and hard-refuse it outright unless the specific side-effecting flag it exists for (--depends-on-add) is also present on the same call. This avoids inventing a second vehicle for 'touch this entry without moving its phase' while keeping the new token unmistakably non-settable as a lifecycle target.

Before constructing a cycle-detection test fixture, trace the FULL transitive dependency graph the fixture change creates, not just the direct edge: adding entry A depends_on entry B when B is already (transitively) depended-upon by other fixture entries can accidentally close a real cycle on an unrelated 'valid edge' test case. Pick a predecessor with no dependents and no outgoing dependencies for the acyclic positive-control case; reserve the entry that already has a reverse edge for the dedicated cycle-refusal case.

A one-paragraph prose addition to a context/patterns doc can trip index-entries.json's own line_count drift check (Rule R) at the next verify-deploy gate 3 run. The remedy script (generate-context-line-counts.sh --write) fixes ALL current drifts in the file, not just the one caused by your own edit -- if the file already carries an unrelated pre-existing drift (e.g. from another task's in-flight edit to a different doc), the script's single run will bundle both fixes into your working tree. Revert the unrelated hunk with a targeted sed/jq edit before committing, so only your own task's entry lands in your commit.
